Thanks Karthik — quick clarifications from our side: 

- When we say PHI not leave our VPC, we mean that the prompt content and model outputs that include patient identifiers must never be stored or accessible in Redwood-hosted logs. Transient processing in memory during inference is fine.
- For auditability, we need request-level metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model used) retained for 12 months, but that metadata must not include prompt text or output content for PHI-labeled requests.
- We will want a signed ack from Redwood that hosted logging can be disabled or that Dedicated/Private deployment guarantees no prompt/output retention.

Can you provide a concrete statement we can hand to Procurement/Security? Also flag any trade-offs (e.g., losing model-quality feedback loop if logs are disabled).

Hi Emma — appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise, shareable statement and then a technical note with trade-offs. Feel free to paste the statement into your procurement questionnaire; we can sign an attestation when you’re ready.

Shareable statement (short)
- Redwood Inference hosted API: by default, non-sensitive request metadata (request id, model, timestamps, error codes) are retained for operational monitoring and troubleshooting for up to 30 days.
- Prompt text and model outputs that contain PII/PHI are not persisted in hosted logs when customers opt into our "no-persist" setting. For customers that require strict residency, Dedicated or Private deployments ensure that prompts and outputs are processed inside the customer tenancy and are not sent to Redwood-hosted storage.
- For customers requiring an auditable 3rd-party retention window, we offer a Dedicated deployment with configurable metadata retention (can be set to 12 months) while still preventing prompt/output content from being stored.

Technical appendix / trade-offs
- Hosted default: 30-day metadata retention; prompt/output retention is opt-in for telemetry & improvement pipelines. If you opt out, we do not persist prompt/output content.
- Disabling prompt/output persistence means Redwood cannot use those examples for model improvement or post-hoc quality analysis; this may slightly slow identification of model regressions but has no impact on inference latency.
- Dedicated/Private: data stays in your VPC/tenant; we can run with zero retention of prompts/outputs and provide KMS-managed keys for any logs we store.
- Logging fields we can retain (without content): request_id, model_name, shard_id, latency_ms, response_code, region, tenant_id, timestamp. We will redact any fields flagged as PHI.

Next steps I propose
- Rishi will send a short technical appendix with sample logging schema and the JSON schema of redaction rules (tomorrow).
- I will route a formal attestation letter you can include with procurement (Legal + Security sign-off) once you confirm Dedicated/Private interest.

Attachments included: redwood_security_factsheet.pdf, medi_core_sla_draft.docx

Let me know if you want the short statement edited for Procurement language — happy to make it more formal.

Best,
Karthik
